newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak central bank says sterilisation moves working.
newsitem.headline: Slovak central bank says sterilisation moves working.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Tuesday its recent moves to sterilise liquidity on the domestic interbank money market were working.

"The (market) situation after the moves we have made so far proves that we are going in the right direction...raising our hopes that the current moves will bring us the desired result," Peter Andresic, head of NBS Open Market Operations, told Reuters.
He added that there were no imminent plans to review the steps, due to the current liquidity shortage on the market.

As of January 1, the NBS stopped quoting securities repo and reverse repo rates, and started to hold tenders on a daily basis, if needed, for limited volumes of short-term securities repurchases instead.
The NBS said that by reducing the refinancing volumes, it hoped to help curb credit expansion which is at the heart of the country's burgeoning money supply.

Slovak interbank money market rates jumped early on Tuesday with overnights hitting 26.4 percent, with dealers saying the banking sector was in a liquidity crunch ahead of Wednesday's minimum reserve deadline.
The currrent overnight rate level is equal to the penalty of three times the country's discount rate, which banks must pay if they fail to meet minimum reserve demands.
Before the NBS tenders began, interbank money market rates ranged around 14.5-16 percent.
"In accordance with our set programme, we intervene on the volume targets to stem the money supply growth, we do not intervene on the banks' minimum resereve fulfillment," Andresic said.
"No big decisions can be expected tomorrow (based on the minimum reserve fulfillment results), one cannot expect us to review or reasssess our moves after 15 days."

Earlier in the day, the NBS held a tender for a one-day securities repurchase, offering banks liquidity at a fixed volume of 2.5 billion crowns, though banks estimated the market was short by 4-5 billion crowns.

Despite the recent boost in the interbank money market rates, local commercial banks said they had no imminent plans to raise their prime rates, with many hoping the NBS would reverse the recent moves and supply market with liquidity.
Prime rates at Slovak banks currently range between 11 and 14.75 percent.
